descript.abstract: These data contain information about scans of geophysical logs and permit file documents regarding oil and gas test well sites drilled in Washington State from 1890 to present. Scanned documents are available in PDF format.
descript.purpose: This dataset was generated to summarize pertinent information regarding oil and gas documents on file at the Washington Department of Natural Resources that were scanned into PDF format and made available to the public. Previously, someone interested in obtaining oil and gas documents would be required to visit the DNR and make paper copies. Links to scanned documents can be found in this dataset along with a description of each document.

procstep.procdesc:
Information was provided to the Division of Geology and Earth Resources by operators and filed. Beginning in 1947, Information Circulars were created from the filed information provided by the operators. Points were created and attributed from information contained in these Information Circulars and addendums. Different methods were used to generate these points. Some were programmatically generated, some approximated using section divisions, and others were electronically measured from section lines. It was known that some of the well locations were in error for two reasons. Firstly, the spreadsheet data came from sources one or more iterations removed from the original data. Original data is located in hard-copy files maintained by the Washington Division of Geology and Earth Resources (Livingston, 1958; McFarland, 1981; McFarland, 1983; oil and gas addendum) pursuant to the Oil and Gas Conservation Act, Chapter 146 (RCW 78.52.001 to 78.52-550), and in hard-copy files for some wells drilled prior to 1954 when the Oil and Gas Conservation Act went into effect. Secondly, the program used to generate the initial latitude-longitude locations did not yield locations as precise as the original file information would allow. Therefore, we reviewed the locations in the hard-copy files and 1) corrected the township, range, section, and within section location data in the spreadsheet, and 2) added information for wells that had been permitted under the Oil and Gas Conservation Act but not drilled. For most records the location in the original hard-copy files is in the form of township, range, section, distance from the north or south section line, and distance from the east or west section line. In other cases, especially for wells drilled prior to the Oil and Gas Conservation Act, that degree of detail is not available. The spreadsheet with the inexact latitude-longitude information but corrected township, range, section, and within-section information was used to create a point feature class. That feature class was loaded into an ArcMap session with a line shapefile showing detailed, precisely-located township, range, and section lines. The location of each well was adjusted to agree with the most precise, corrected, township, range, section, within-section location and correct latitudes and longitudes calculated.
Version History
Version 3.3 (July, 2016) More complete attribution is provided. Records for scanned documents which are not associated with any drilled well have been removed.
Version 3.2 (August, 2014) Undrilled wells were removed for clarity and attributes were edited for consistency and accuracy.
Version 3.1 (May, 2012) The field WELL_STATUS was fully attributed to describe more clearly the status of the well based upon the contents of the documents on file with the Washington Division of Geology and Earth Resources, namely if the well was drilled or not drilled. In addition, attributes were edited for grammar and consistency.
Version 3.0 (May, 2011) The location of the features within this dataset were checked against the original hard-copy files maintained by the Washington Division of Geology and Earth Resources and corrected accordingly using the process described above, in addition to addition of some boreholes that were permitted but never drilled, and some verification of other attributes.
Version 2.0 (June, 2010) This dataset was migrated from a shapefile to a feature class within a geodatabase. Feature class names and attribute names were changed, and metadata for the entire dataset was updated.
Version 1.0 (October, 2008) Original data in shapefile format.

enttyp.enttypd: Permit files include scans of official State documents issued to oil and gas permit holders, or forms/data summaries included in the permit holder's data submission to the permitting agency (Washington Department of Natural Resources) regarding the permitted borehole. Examples include: Well Record and History, Intent to Drill or Deepen, and Driller's Logs. Geophysical logs include recordings of numerous types of physical and geophysical properties along a specified length of a oil and gas borehole. Examples include: Gamma Ray Logs, Electrical Logs, and Cement Bond Logs. This dataset includes a link to each scanned file and other attributes of the documents, such as logged depth, log date, and temperature.
